newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile has no plans to sell copper firm Enami.
newsitem.headline: Chile has no plans to sell copper firm Enami.

text.p: The Chilean government has no plans to privatize state copper mining company Enami which operates two copper smelters, said Enami vice president Claudio Agostini.
Asked if this meant that the government had ruled out any sale, Agostini replied: "It (privatization) has never been considered."
Local media said the government has set up a special commission to study the sale of the firms which runs the Ventanas and Paipote smelting and refining complexes.
The reports said that local copper company Punta del Cobre and Phelps Dodge, which owns the nearby Candelaria copper mine, were interested in joint ventures with Enami.

Agostini said the commission's only task is to set out government policy towards small mining companies which receive aid from the Empresa Nacional de Mineria (Enami) and has not discussed any sell-off.
"The commission is defining government policy towards the small and medium-sized mining industry," he told reporters.
Enami has not been contacted by any private companies regarding joint ventures with the state firm, he added.
Under its $150 million modernization program, Enami sees its output of refined copper output growing to 328,000 tonnes by 1999 from 214,000 tonnes this year.
Its smelted copper production should rise to 204,000 tonnes in 1999 from 190,000 tonnes this year.
